## Summary

Fixes #39.

When `lino-i18n` was run through the npm bin symlink (`npx lino-i18n …`, `node_modules/.bin/lino-i18n …`, or an npm script), it did nothing and exited 0. That meant `lino-i18n check` always passed.

### Root cause

`isCliEntryPoint()` in `js/bin/lino-i18n.js` compared `process.argv[1]` with `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`. Node keeps the symlink path in `process.argv[1]`, but `import.meta.url` is the resolved real path. The two never matched, so `runCli` never ran.

### Fix

- `isCliEntryPoint()` now runs `fs.realpathSync` on both paths before comparing them. This also covers macOS, where `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`. The function is exported, with the paths as overridable parameters, so it can be unit-tested.
- Added a changeset (`patch`) to release the fix.

## How to reproduce (before the fix)

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/l && cd /tmp/l && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm i lino-i18n@0.5.0 >/dev/null
mkdir locales && printf 'en\n  a\n    b "x"\nru\n  a\n    c "y"\n' > locales/ui.lino
npx lino-i18n check --dir locales --reference en; echo "exit $?"   # (no output) exit 0
```

With the patched `bin/lino-i18n.js` copied into that install, the same command prints `# ru / missing: a.b / unknown: a.c` and exits `2`. `npx lino-i18n --version` prints `0.5.0`.

## Tests

New file `js/tests/cli-symlink.test.js`:
- Creates `<tmp>/.bin/lino-i18n -> bin/lino-i18n.js`, the same layout npm uses.
- Spawns `node <symlink> check …` and asserts exit code `2` and the missing/unknown output. Also checks that `node <symlink> --help` prints the usage text.
- Unit-tests `isCliEntryPoint` with a symlink, the real path, a missing path, an unrelated path and `undefined`.
- If the OS refuses to create symlinks (Windows without Developer Mode), the test returns early. On such systems npm uses cmd shims, so the bug cannot happen there.

Against the old `bin/lino-i18n.js`, the spawn test fails (`actual: 0, expected: 2`). With the fix, it passes, along with the existing `tests/cli.test.js`.
title: fix: run CLI when invoked through the npm bin symlink

Adds opt-in recursive loading for layouts such as `locales/`, `locales/prompts/`, and `locales/prompts/system/`. Calling `loadLocalesFromDirectory(root, { recursive: true })` now merges every nested `.lino` catalog by its declared locale, including files containing multiple languages.

Symlinks are skipped to avoid directory cycles; read and parse errors propagate.

Includes usage and collision documentation, TypeScript declarations for both the main and `/loaders` entry points, and a minor-release changeset.

### Reproduction and regression coverage

Create `en.lino` with a UI key and `prompts/system/en.lino` with an instruction key, then call the directory loader with `{ recursive: true }`. Previously only the UI key appeared; both now appear in the English catalog.

All six now pass, covering mixed/nested locales, fallback and both interpolation syntaxes, deterministic duplicate precedence, alias options and explicit-key precedence, ignored files, symlink cycles, and errors. Fixes #29.

Rust publishing currently reads only long-lived token secrets. The automatic release, manual instant release, and standalone release preflight now try the pinned crates.io OIDC authentication action first, with `id-token: write` and the existing `crates.io` environment. Each credential consumer uses `OIDC token || CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || CARGO_TOKEN`, as required by the October 13 policy update. Authentication failure permits fallback; neither secret is deleted. Automatic authentication uses the same release condition as its preflight/publish steps, and credentials are checked before versioning.

The existing archive-free preflight remains in place and checks both crates using the selected credential. Each job authenticates independently; short-lived tokens are never shared between jobs. There is no reusable workflow interface requiring `workflow_call` secrets. A Rust patch fragment prepares the next release.

[Publishing documentation](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-29-f60a045533b2/docs/crates-io-publishing.md) records the identity for both crates: `link-foundation/lino-i18n`, top-level workflow `rust.yml`, environment `crates.io`. An idempotent registration helper preserves existing publishers and verifies writes by reading them back.

Reproduction and verification:

- Before the fix, `python3 experiments/issue-29-crates-auth.py` failed for all three missing OIDC permissions and for selecting a stored token ahead of an available OIDC token.
- The regression now passes eight tests covering action order, permissions, matching conditions, ordered fallback, the real shell preflight against a local registry, missing credentials, either crate being denied, and idempotent publisher registration/readback. Workflows CI runs it and watches both experiment files.
- Local Rust workspace tests with all features, Clippy, formatting, Node/Bun/Deno suites (187 tests each), TypeScript checks, shared Node tests (48), workflow policy, actionlint, documentation checks, secrets scanning and Cargo audit pass. All 17 executable Rust helpers, release/validation fixtures, nine Chromium tests, production builds/browser tests for Next.js (four tests) and TanStack (two tests), and npm/Cargo packaging checks also pass.
- Current-main Security run [40319781824](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40319781824) failed its npm audit on Next.js, undici, zod and fast-uri (downloaded log lines 166–205). Next.js is patched from 16.4.0 to 16.4.3 and compatible transitive patches are locked; npm audit now reports zero vulnerabilities. A JS patch changeset records this CI prerequisite.
- Online zizmor found the previous `rust-toolchain` SHA had been detached by the generated `stable` branch rewrite. All uses now pin the action's reachable `v1` commit and retain their explicit toolchain inputs; the online audit passes.

**Blocked acceptance criterion — register and verify trusted publishers for both crates.** The [live credential job](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40684220445/job/122802368151) used the existing organization `CARGO_TOKEN` available to this repository. Registration inspection returned HTTP 403 for **both** crates (downloaded job log lines 184–185). The pinned action successfully obtained the GitHub JWT, but crates.io refused the exchange with HTTP 400: “No Trusted Publishing config found for repository `link-foundation/lino-i18n`” (lines 202–204). The subsequent stored-token preflight passed for **both** crates without uploading an archive (lines 220–221), verifying the fallback on GitHub Actions.

Neither trusted publisher is claimed as registered, and OIDC-only authorization remains unverified. An individual crate owner must register the documented identity for both crates in crates.io settings, or run the included helper with an owner token that permits the `trusted-publishing` endpoint for both crates. The available publishing token cannot access that endpoint; no local Cargo credential or second repository-accessible Cargo secret is available. After registration, rerun the main-branch release preflight and confirm the OIDC exchange and both crate checks succeed before considering this criterion complete. The temporary branch-only setup trigger was removed in the final workflow, and all existing main-branch publication guards are restored. No release was published and neither secret was deleted.

All five workflows pass at commit `f3d6c6b` (created 2026-10-28 12:05:50 UTC, after the latest commit): [Documentation](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40685046226), [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40685046183), [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40685046299), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40685046266), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/40685046110). The completed diagnostic registration job is preserved above; its redundant older-commit downstream workflow was cancelled after evidence collection.

**This PR remains draft and unmerged because registration and real OIDC-only authorization for both crates are still unfinished.** Ready-for-review promotion is held with that external acceptance criterion.

The original token-deleting migration step is superseded by the later policy; it will not be run. Addresses the React and code-only authoring gaps in issue #25: applications can author source messages, ICU and rich JSX over `.lino` catalogs, extract those messages without executing application code, and use isolated state for SSR and hydration. Existing keyed JS/browser APIs and Rust macros remain covered by regression tests.

The [pinned GT case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-25-e2b4af9aea1e/docs/case-studies/issue-25/README.md), [requirement matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-25-e2b4af9aea1e/docs/case-studies/issue-25/REQUIREMENTS.md) and [verification record](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-25-e2b4af9aea1e/docs/case-studies/issue-25/VERIFICATION.md) contain the research, reproductions and remaining implementation plans. This PR does not close #25: entire GT ecosystem parity remains incomplete.

## Changes

- Source descriptors, tagged templates, full FormatJS ICU, dictionaries, locale configuration, lazy/versioned catalogs and request snapshots; optional Rust ICU with the existing default MSRV preserved.
- React source `T`, named variables, branches, derivation and Intl formatting; scoped Node/server access; an opt-in JSX/attribute compiler and bounded module-aware extraction through the CLI and Vite/Rollup.
- Optional Next App Router, TanStack Start, Vue/SFC and injected Native Text adapters, with actual framework fixtures, isolated SSR, hydration, locale navigation and persistence.
- Published GT SDK, Markdown and locale-registry bridges; bounded Python AST extraction; actual rrweb recording/replay with protected variable values; scope-aware ESLint diagnostics and explicit variable suggestions.
- Minor release fragments for JS and Rust, runnable examples, pinned research/checksums/license, screenshots and CI coverage for the adapters.

## Reproduction and validation

On the base revision, the source-message/server/tooling exports were absent. Reproductions also found lost quoted/prototype catalog keys, incomplete compiled ICU conversion, mismatched JSX extraction identities, stale-source review failures, overlapping-request and locale-load hazards, and incorrect React currency children. The corresponding automated regressions are listed in the verification record.

Actual upstream probes reproduced Python shadowing/malformed-syntax defects, replay variable fallback corruption, regenerated Sanity span keys and silently skipped target blocks. Shipped tests verify Python and replay fixes. The Sanity candidate tests passed, but the candidate was reverted for the dependency-review failure documented below.

Local validation:

- 187 tests each in Node, Bun and Deno; five strict TypeScript configurations.
- Nine Chromium scenarios, four production Next scenarios and two production Start scenarios.
- Cargo all-feature tests/doctests, default-feature Rust 1.87 tests, rustfmt and Clippy.
- Lint, formatting, duplication, secrets, documentation, workflow policy, dependency pins, file limits and clean core npm audit.

All five CI workflows passed for final revision `2245c82`, created after its 2026-10-08 23:16 UTC commit: [Documentation](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37858546395), [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37858546522), [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37858546357), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37858546416), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37858546347). The JS OS/runtime/Node matrix, strict types, production browser/framework fixtures, Rust/MSRV and security jobs ran successfully.

## Remaining limits

No GT project or live CMS credentials were available: hosted jobs/CDN/publication and authenticated Studio permissions/UI are unverified. Native device/emulator behavior, broader deployment/router configurations, Python runtime/imported helper graphs, GT descriptor/wire compatibility and agent/daemon protocols remain outside the shipped coverage, with plans in the matrix.

**Sanity integration is deferred.** Its seven actual GT/Sanity contract tests and consumer types passed in [candidate CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37857389183), but [dependency review failed](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/actions/runs/37857389186/job/113584744669) on unpatched braces 3.0.3 (downloaded full log lines 4360–4362). The current compatible toolchain still includes it. A forward-moving revert removed the integration and fixture without weakening security gates. [The investigation](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-25-e2b4af9aea1e/docs/sanity.md) preserves reproductions, candidate commit, 19 upstream advisories and the resumption plan. The shipped package has no Sanity export; core audits clean and its five type configurations retain strict library checks.

## Visual evidence

The currency regression includes actual before/after screenshots. The other images show the working French examples; their English counterparts are in the verification record.

Fixes #26.

This brings every dependency in every ecosystem of the repository up to its latest version and adds Dependabot so the drift does not build up again. Each value was resolved from its registry on 2026-10-08. Items that can't move have a written reason.

The full [requirement matrix, per-ecosystem before/after tables, majors crossed and left-behind reasons](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-26-f68d85bd297d/dev/log/issues/26/pulls/27/ANALYSIS.md), the [primary sources](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-26-f68d85bd297d/dev/log/issues/26/pulls/27/SOURCES.md), registry snapshots, before/after logs and archived CI logs are committed under `dev/log/issues/26/pulls/27/`.

## What changed

| Ecosystem | Change |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript | `npm-check-updates -u` and a lockfile regenerated from scratch. links-notation 0.13 → 0.23, lino-objects-codec 0.4 → 0.9, plus @playwright/test, @types/node, @types/react, eslint, eslint-plugin-prettier, prettier and react. `engines.node` goes from `>=20.0.0` to `>=22.11.0`: lino-objects-codec 0.9 requires it, and Node 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30. CI tests Node 22.x (the floor), 24.x and 26.x. `npm outdated` is empty |
| Rust | Edition 2021 → 2024; `rust-version` 1.75 → 1.87, the measured minimum (1.85/1.86 fail inside links-notation 0.23); resolver 2 → 3 (MSRV-aware). lino-objects-codec 0.2 → 0.8, syn 2 → 3, and proc-macro2/quote floors at the resolved versions. Every `Cargo.lock` entry is at its latest version. A new Rust 1.87 CI leg tests the MSRV |
| rust-script helpers | ureq 2 → 3 in four helpers (the new config, header, error and body API). toml 0.8 → 1 in `check-version-modification.rs`: the old `Value` parsing idiom still compiles under toml 1 but rejects every manifest at runtime, so it now parses a `toml::Table` and has a unit test. All `//!` cargo floors equal the resolved versions |
| Python | PyYAML is already at the latest 6.0.3. The policy job now pins CPython 3.14 through `actions/setup-python@v7` |
| GitHub Actions | checkout, setup-node and upload-artifact v6 → v7. install-action moves to v2.87.26 and Deno to 2.9.7. Every hash pin carries its version comment. Runners: ubuntu-24.04 → ubuntu-26.04 and macos-15 → macos-26 (windows-2025 is already the newest). `.github/actionlint.yaml` declares ubuntu-26.04 because actionlint 1.7.12 predates it |
| Automation | `.github/dependabot.yml` covers npm `/js`, cargo `/rust` (the workspace root also fetches both members and the lock), pip `/scripts`, and github-actions `/` plus `/.github/actions/*`. Updates run weekly, grouped per ecosystem, with a 7-day cooldown that zizmor now audits. `scripts/check-dependency-pins.py` runs in the Workflows policy job and fails if an action or tool is pinned at two versions, or if the MSRV or Node floor leg is missing |
| Release | JS changeset (minor, because the supported Node range shrinks) and Rust changelog fragment (minor) |

## Left behind, with reasons

- **npm recovery pin (stays on 11.21.0; npm 12.2.0 exists):** every supported Node line bundles npm 11, and trusted publishing only needs 11.5.1+.
- **lino-arguments (stays on 0.3.0, the latest on npm):** its 0.4.0 release failed upstream, so its links-notation 0.11 / yargs 17 subtree stays. Reported as [lino-arguments#41](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments/issues/41).
- **61 transitive npm majors:** their parents are already at their latest versions and exclude the new majors.
- **actionlint workarounds:** a label entry for ubuntu-26.04 (rhysd/actionlint#682) and the existing `queue` ignore (rhysd/actionlint#657) stay until upstream releases a fix.
- **MSRV:** links-notation doesn't declare its real MSRV. Reported as [links-notation#334](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/334).
- **Hand-written `.lino` catalogue parsers:** they stay. The experiments show that `parseIndented`, `decode` and the links-notation `Parser` don't preserve this dialect's escapes and `"""` blocks.

## Reproductions and verification

- `experiments/issue-26-toml-document-parse.rs` reproduces the toml 1 runtime defect, and a unit test in the helper covers it.
- `experiments/issue-26-ureq3-registry-state.rs` exercises the ureq 3 port against live crates.io.
- `experiments/issue-26-dependency-pins.py` proves that each kind of drift fails the new guard.
- Local runs are green:
  - 61 JS tests on Node 22 and 24, plus types, lint, format, duplication, secrets and pack.
  - Rust fmt, Clippy, tests and doctests on 1.87 and 1.99.
  - All 16 standalone rust-script helpers (with the shared modules they include) checked and tested with `-Dwarnings`.
  - Workflow policy, pin guard, actionlint and zizmor (pedantic).
- `npm audit`, `cargo audit` (including the helper lock trees) and `pip-audit` report no vulnerabilities.
- CI on every pushed commit passes all five workflows, with no warning or error annotations. The results and archived logs are in [FINAL-VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-26-f68d85bd297d/dev/log/issues/26/pulls/27/FINAL-VERIFICATION.md).
- Two CI incidents, both recorded in FINAL-VERIFICATION.md:
  - The first evidence commit had log names containing `:`, which Windows checkout rejects. They were renamed, and windows-2025 now checks out and passes.
  - Some macos-26 jobs were never assigned a GitHub-hosted runner ("not acquired by Runner of type hosted"). They ran no code, no GitHub incident was open, and they passed once re-run.
- The unused composite action `.github/actions/publish-dockerhub` is called by no workflow, so CI doesn't run it. Its docker actions are already at their latest majors.

Fixes #23.

The reported Rust release staged version files before rebasing a concurrently advanced main, then failed with a dirty-index error. The JavaScript release published an accepted version again while registry readback was still invisible, producing staged-version E409 errors. Releases now synchronize validated metadata while clean, serialize all eight writers without replacing pending jobs, and require verified registry visibility after an accepted publication. Source drift, invalid refs, malformed fragments, fragment cleanup failures and failed Actions output writes fail explicitly.

The same review covers the whole codebase: complete PR change detection and workspace/member version guards; strict locked installs; zero-warning lint/helper compilation; dependency audits; secrets, workflow and documentation checks; guarded manual releases; complete terminal status gates; supported runners and pinned tools. Both documentation publishers assemble the complete JS/Rust site. Existing public APIs, supported package runtime engines, release modes and npm recovery are preserved. JS and Rust patch fragments prepare the next release.

The full [investigation, requirement matrix, timeline and solution alternatives](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-23-bc288e2f1144/dev/log/issues/23/pulls/24/ANALYSIS.md), [599-file template comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-23-bc288e2f1144/dev/log/issues/23/pulls/24/TEMPLATE-COMPARISON.md), [primary sources](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/blob/issue-23-bc288e2f1144/dev/log/issues/23/pulls/24/SOURCES.md), historical logs and before/after verification evidence are committed under `dev/log/issues/23/pulls/24/`. - `experiments/issue-23-publish-baseline.mjs` replays the original duplicate publication; five publisher unit tests verify accepted/invisible, staged-conflict, visibility, error and exhaustion behavior.
- `experiments/issue-23-rust-release.py` executes the real release helper against a local bare remote with a concurrent JS metadata commit and verifies consumed fragments, workspace/path dependency versions, locks and the remote tag with its existing description/label fields. JS tests cover the reciprocal race and detached checkout.

CodeQL loads both the product and seventeen-target helper manifests without the prior semantic-analysis warnings. Repeated evidence archiving preserves its index, and Workflows CI additionally verifies every archived record/log checksum. The final evidence commit receives a fresh complete CI validation recorded below and in the PR checks.
- Check-run annotation review caught six expected-negative-test diagnostics displayed as errors in an otherwise passing Rust run. Captured fixture messages now render as plain text, while real guard failures retain their annotations. The before/after regression executes all five real CI fixtures, asserts their statuses and rejects leaked workflow commands; Rust CI runs it instead of the prior direct fixture invocation.
